title: Linear vs Angular Motion

competencies.text: Differentiate translational motion from rotational motion.
Relate linear quantities (displacement, velocity, acceleration) to angular quantities (angular displacement, angular velocity, angular acceleration).

days.title: Two Ways Things Move
days.content:
🎯 Learning Target

This week you will differentiate translational from rotational motion and relate linear quantities to angular quantities.

🚶 Translational Motion

In translational motion, every part of an object moves the same distance in the same direction at the same time. An elevator going up, a box sliding across the floor and a jeepney on a straight road are examples.

🌀 Rotational Motion

In rotational motion, an object turns around an axis. Every point moves in a circle around that axis. A ceiling fan, the hands of a clock and a spinning top rotate. Points far from the axis travel a bigger circle in the same time, so they move faster than points near it.

⚽ Both at Once: Rolling

Many objects do both. A ball rolling down a ramp moves forward (its center translates) while it spins around its center (it rotates). A bicycle wheel on the road does the same. Earth also does both: it revolves around the Sun and rotates on its axis.

MotionWhat every point doesExample
TranslationalMoves the same distance, same directionElevator, sliding box
RotationalMoves in a circle around an axisFan blade, clock hand
Rolling (both)Center moves forward while the body spinsRolling ball, moving tire

✅ Quick Check

Answer 3 questions and read the explanation after each.

scenario.text: Which of these shows PURELY translational motion?

choices.label: A box sliding across a smooth floor
A ball rolling across the smooth floor
A ceiling fan blade turning in place
A door swinging open on its hinges

scenario.explanation: When a box slides without tipping, every part of it moves the same distance in the same direction. The ball rolls (translates and rotates), the fan blade rotates, and the door rotates about its hinges.

scenario.text: A tricycle tire rolls along a road without slipping. How does it move?

choices.label: It translates and rotates at the same time
It only translates forward along the road
It only rotates around its axle, in place
It neither translates nor rotates at all

scenario.explanation: The tire's center moves forward (translation) while the tire spins around the axle (rotation). Rolling is always a combination of both.

scenario.text: On a turning merry-go-round, which rider travels the LONGEST path in one turn?

choices.label: The rider sitting at the outer edge
The rider sitting near the center
All riders travel exactly the same path
The rider standing right on the axis

scenario.explanation: In one turn every rider sweeps the same angle, but a rider farther from the axis goes around a bigger circle, so the path (and the speed) is greater at the edge.

days.title: Angular Quantities
days.content:
📐 Measuring Rotation

To describe rotation we use angular quantities. They tell how much and how fast something turns — not how far a point travels.

  • Angular displacement (θ) — the angle turned, measured in radians (rad). One full turn = 2π rad (about 6.28 rad) = 360°.
  • Angular velocity (ω) — how fast the angle changes, in rad/s. A fan at 60 revolutions per minute (rpm) turns once per second, so ω = 2π rad/s ≈ 6.28 rad/s.
  • Angular acceleration (α) — how fast ω changes, in rad/s². A fan speeding up after you switch it on has angular acceleration.

🔁 Linear Partners

Linear (straight-line)Angular (turning)
Displacement d (m)Angular displacement θ (rad)
Velocity v (m/s)Angular velocity ω (rad/s)
Acceleration a (m/s²)Angular acceleration α (rad/s²)
💡 Remember: every point of a rigid turning object has the same angular velocity, but not the same linear speed.

🔗 Activity 1 — Match the Pairs

Match each quantity or idea to its meaning or example. Read the reason that appears for each correct pair. You need 70%; retakes are unlimited.

match.why: It describes how much an object has turned, not how far a point traveled.
It tells how fast the angle changes each second.

match.right: Change in turning rate, in rad/s²
match.why: A fan speeding up or slowing down has angular acceleration.
The circumference is 2π times the radius, so one turn sweeps 2π rad.
60 rpm is 1 turn per second, and 1 turn is 2π ≈ 6.28 rad.

match.right: Distance per second along a path
match.why: It is measured in m/s and depends on how far the point is from the axis.

match.right: Line that the body turns around
match.why: Every point of a rotating body moves in a circle around this line.

match.right: All points of a turning rigid wheel
match.why: The whole wheel turns through the same angle in the same time.

days.title: Linking Linear and Angular Motion
days.content:
🔗 The Bridge: Radius

The distance r from the axis connects turning to straight-line motion:

d = r × θ    v = r × ω    a = r × α

Angles must be in radians for these to work.

📝 Worked Example 1

A bicycle wheel (r = 0.35 m) turns at ω = 10 rad/s. The speed of a point on the tire is v = r × ω = 0.35 × 10 = 3.5 m/s. If the tire does not slip, the bicycle also moves at 3.5 m/s.

📝 Worked Example 2

A fan blade turns at ω = 20 rad/s. A point 0.10 m from the center moves at 2 m/s; the blade tip, 0.25 m from the center, moves at 5 m/s. Same ω, bigger r → bigger v. That is why the blade tips are the most dangerous part.

⚠️ Common Mistakes

  • Dividing instead of multiplying (v = ω ÷ r is wrong).
  • Using degrees or rpm without converting to radians or rad/s.
  • Thinking points closer to the axis turn faster — they turn at the same ω but move slower.

🎯 Activity 2 — Scenario Challenge

Apply the formulas and reason about real situations. Read every explanation. You need 70%; retakes are unlimited.

scenario.text: A windmill blade turns at 2 rad/s. Its tip is 8 m from the hub. How fast does the tip move?
scenario.explanation: v = r × ω = 8 m × 2 rad/s = 16 m/s. 4 m/s comes from dividing (8 ÷ 2), 10 m/s from adding, and 0.25 m/s from dividing the wrong way.

scenario.text: A jeepney tire (radius 0.4 m) rolls without slipping while turning at 25 rad/s. How fast is the jeepney moving?
scenario.explanation: For rolling without slipping the vehicle's speed equals the tire's rim speed: v = 0.4 × 25 = 10 m/s.

scenario.text: Two marks are drawn on a turning electric-fan blade: P at 5 cm and Q at 20 cm from the center. Which statement is correct?

choices.label: Q moves 4 times as fast as P
P moves 4 times as fast as Q
Both move at the same linear speed
Q turns with 4 times P's angular velocity

scenario.explanation: Both marks share the same ω. Since v = rω and Q is 4 times farther from the axis, Q's linear speed is 4 times P's.

scenario.text: A golfer wants a faster club-head speed without swinging her arms any faster. Which change works?

choices.label: Use a longer club at the same swing rate
Use a shorter club at the same swing rate
Hold the club closer to the club head
Swing the club in a much smaller circle

scenario.explanation: The club head's speed is v = rω. Keeping ω the same but increasing r (a longer club) increases v. A shorter club or a smaller circle reduces r.

scenario.text: A washing machine drum speeds up from rest to 120 rad/s in 10 s. What is its average angular acceleration?
scenario.explanation: α = change in ω ÷ time = (120 − 0) ÷ 10 = 12 rad/s². Multiplying gives 1,200 and dividing the wrong way gives 0.083.

days.title: Rotation in Machines and Nature
days.content:
⚙️ Gears and Chains

When two gears are linked by a chain, the chain moves at the same linear speed on both gears. A small gear must turn faster (larger ω) than a large gear to keep up, because v = rω. On a bicycle, a big front gear turning slowly can make a small rear gear — and the wheel — turn quickly.

🚲 Wheels Turn Rotation into Travel

Every turn of a rolling wheel moves the vehicle forward by one circumference (2πr). Bigger wheels cover more distance per turn.

🌍 Earth's Two Motions

Earth rotates once a day (day and night) and revolves around the Sun once a year (seasons and the yearly calendar). A person at the equator is carried around a much bigger circle than a person near the poles, so they move faster — even though both rotate with the same ω.

🧠 Reasoning Tip

Before choosing an answer, ask two questions: "Is the angular velocity the same for both points?" and "Which point is farther from the axis?" These two questions solve most rotation problems.

🔐 Formative Check — Escape the Lab

3 lives, 6 keys. You need 70% (5 of 6). Read the explanation after every question.

escape.text: Which quantity is measured in rad/s?
escape.explanation: Angular velocity is the angle turned per second, so its unit is radians per second (rad/s).

escape.text: A wheel of radius 0.3 m turns at 6 rad/s. What is the speed of a point on its rim?
escape.explanation: v = r × ω = 0.3 × 6 = 1.8 m/s. The other answers come from dividing or adding the numbers.

escape.text: A bicycle chain links a large front gear and a small rear gear. Which turns with the GREATER angular velocity?
escape.explanation: The chain moves at the same linear speed on both gears. With v = rω, the gear with the smaller radius must have the larger ω.

escape.text: Which pair correctly matches a linear quantity with its angular partner?
escape.explanation: Each linear quantity has an angular partner: displacement ↔ θ, velocity ↔ ω, acceleration ↔ α.

escape.text: Ana stands at the equator and Ben stands near the North Pole. As Earth rotates, which statement is TRUE?

choices.label: Same angular velocity, but Ana moves faster
Same linear speed, but Ben turns faster
Ben moves faster because he is farther north
Ana turns through a larger angle each day

escape.explanation: Both turn once a day (same ω). Ana is much farther from Earth's axis, so her circle is bigger and her linear speed is greater.

escape.text: A tire with radius 0.5 m rolls without slipping for 10 full turns. About how far does the vehicle travel?
escape.explanation: Each turn moves the vehicle one circumference: 2πr = 2 × 3.14 × 0.5 ≈ 3.14 m. Ten turns ≈ 31 m. 63 m would need a radius of 1 m.
